note: Voice variety from staffs with their own drone, each block the same job (hear the landing note, then leap) in a new key and scale: a short leap drill that starts eased (A major keeps the staff low, sung on "oo") and then opens the full range in F major, made-up calls and answers in minor, then a made-up tune in Mixolydian. Each staff shows only the notes in play, labelled by degree as the text names them; only the first block is a bare drill.

exercise.title: 4ths and 5ths in three scales
exercise.focus: Leaps of a 4th and 5th over a drone · A major low, F major high · D minor · G Mixolydian
exercise.why: A leap lands in tune when you hear the landing note before you sing it, so every block is the same job in a new scale: hear it, then leap.

sections.text: Low in A, then high in F

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. Sing {{1}} up to {{4}}, then {{1}} up to {{5}}, on "oo", which keeps your voice light. Hear the landing note in your head before each leap, then check where your line lands.

Now press Play and Start microphone on the F staff below, which runs your whole range. The notes change, the pattern doesn't: sing the same leaps from the low {{1}} on "ah", then from the high {{1}} on "oo".

Press Start exercise below to start the drone on D and the mic. The same leaps now sit in D minor, with {{b3}} added. Make up a short call on "oo" that leaps up from {{1}}, then answer it on "ee" with a different leap that ends on {{1}}.
G Mixolydian: make up a tune

Press Start exercise below to start the drone on G and the mic. Make up a short tune from {{1}}, {{4}}, {{5}} and {{b7}}, leaping between them in any order, and move through the vowels "ee-oh-oo-oh-ah" as you go. When a leap misses, sing just that leap again slowly, then put it back in the tune.
